title: Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Bookings Open, Fares Start at Rs 2,810
excerpt: The first regular train leaves Bengaluru at 7:45 p.m. on November 3 and Mumbai on November 2, with confirmed berths only and full-route fares from Rs 2,810 to Rs 4,450.
body:
• Bookings are open for the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper, with the first regular train from SMVT Bengaluru, 27652, departing at 7:45 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and the first regular train from Mumbai, 27651, departing CSMT at 8:10 p.m. on Monday, November 2.
  • Full-route fares are Rs 2,810 in AC 3-Tier, Rs 3,630 in AC 2-Tier and Rs 4,450 in AC First Class, as reported by The Indian Express when bookings opened on October 31.
  • Book on the IRCTC website or the Rail Connect and RailOne apps, or at a Passenger Reservation System counter - only confirmed berths are sold, with no RAC or waiting list, so a sold-out train has no waitlist to join.
  • The overnight service covers the route in about 16 hours, against 22 to 24 hours on existing trains, and runs six days a week.

Ticket bookings have opened for the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper Express, the overnight service linking Sir M Visvesvaraya Terminal (SMVT) in Bengaluru with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) in Mumbai. The Indian Express reported the fares and the start of bookings on the morning of October 31, 2026, and the first regular departures follow within days: train 27651 leaves CSMT Mumbai at 8:10 p.m. on Monday, November 2, and train 27652 leaves SMVT Bengaluru at 7:45 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, according to the timetable reported by Deccan Herald and cited by NewsPlainly. An inaugural special is scheduled to run from Bengaluru on Sunday, November 1.

Fares and how to book

The fare for the full SMVT Bengaluru to CSMT Mumbai journey is Rs 2,810 in AC 3-Tier, Rs 3,630 in AC 2-Tier and Rs 4,450 in AC First Class, The Indian Express reported. The train has 16 coaches offering the three AC classes. Passengers can book through the IRCTC website, the Rail Connect and RailOne mobile applications, or at Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counters at stations. A fuller breakdown of the launch timetable and booking rules is in the HelloRail booking report.

Booking rules differ from most long-distance trains. Under the Railway Board fare framework reported by NewsPlainly, only confirmed tickets are issued for Vande Bharat sleeper services - there is no RAC, no waiting list and no partly confirmed tickets. A minimum chargeable distance of 400 km also applies, so even a short hop is charged as 400 km. HelloRail reported the same confirmed-only position, with no RAC or Tatkal provision for this service.

Timings, running days and stops

Train 27652 departs SMVT Bengaluru at 7:45 p.m. and reaches CSMT Mumbai at 11:55 a.m. the next day, a journey of about 16 hours on a route where existing trains take 22 to 24 hours, Deccan Herald reported. The service runs six days a week: there is no departure from Bengaluru on Mondays and no departure from Mumbai on Tuesdays, which is why the first regular departures from the two ends fall on different dates. Reported halts on the route include Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan. Travellers should confirm the stop list and intermediate fares for their exact journey on IRCTC before paying, because reports read for this article did not publish a complete station-to-station fare table.

Why the route matters

Bengaluru-Mumbai is one of the busiest inter-city corridors in southern and western India, used heavily by technology and finance professionals, students and families - including diaspora travellers who land in one city and continue to the other. An overnight train that boards after the working day and arrives before noon the next day competes directly with late-evening flights once airport transfers and early check-in times are counted. Demand at launch was strong: HelloRail reported that Second AC and First AC had already sold out for the inaugural day of service by the afternoon of October 31. Because there is no waiting list, travellers who miss out on their preferred date or class will need to pick another date rather than queue for a berth.

What to check before you travel

Check the train number and direction carefully - 27652 runs Bengaluru to Mumbai and 27651 runs Mumbai to Bengaluru - and remember the weekly off-days when planning a return. Fares for intermediate journeys are shown during an IRCTC search for that station pair. Reports differed on whether the published full-route fare includes onboard meals, so readers should check the fare details displayed at booking rather than assume catering is included.
